findings.title: Require observed session identity before accepting cleanup
findings.body: The new scenario requires reconciliation before cleanup of the observed identity (scenario_prompt lines 461-467), but this check accepts any successful sessions request after interruption, even after deletion. Starting from the new passing unit fixture, move delete-session from 3.5 to 2.5 seconds and keep sessions at 3: the same completed post-timeout call contains both, all new checks still accept, and global cleanup checks only inspect deletion and final inactivity. A blind deletion followed by an empty sessions listing can therefore pass without first observing the session identity. Require a reconciliation that exposes the created identity before its DELETE, and add a negative ordering case.

findings.title: Isolate the pending-response condition in the negative test
findings.body: The new response-still-pending regression changes timeout to 4, while the evaluator independently requires timeout == 1. Its rejection assertion therefore succeeds even if response_was_pending is removed entirely, leaving the intended delayed-response false positive unprotected. Keep timeout at 1 for the already-returned-response negative case, with completion after the delay boundary; test rejection of timeout 4 separately.

gaps.detail: The delayed-create scenario models a returned AMKernel cell timeout, not a missing MCP terminal response, transport disconnection or outer Agent expiry. Those documentation distinctions are not jointly exercised by this new scenario.
Same-kernel process-boundary cleanup unit is a dictionary mutation, not official-Client driver.quit or restoration; separate end-to-end execution is needed for that seam.

Harness proxy rejects GET /sessions (appium_proxy.py:715-719); synthetic fixture exposes it. Skill only calls for an available endpoint or retained identity, so this is not a documentation contradiction or AMKernel core defect. RecoveryRuntime creates a fresh Runtime and only reclaims proxy-confirmed identities; it cannot recover old Python objects.
